messages:
maria: Heads up — I want to propose sunsetting the legacy `latency-band` heuristic in favor of the new unified scorer (cost+latency). Short rationale in the next message.

sam: +1 curious about migration impact on Dedicated customers who tuned their latency-band thresholds.

kevin: real quick: the old heuristic is heavily used by edge routes and some customer configs. We need a compatibility shim for tenant-level overrides.

maria: Agreed. Rationale: `latency-band` is brittle with mixed workloads (short chat vs long generation). The unified scorer normalizes token-cost and p95 latency into a single score -> more stable routing and fewer oscillations. Also gives us a single knob for A/B experiments.

jamie: Sounds good. Any perf numbers we can share?

maria: From the sim runs: unified scorer reduced routing-induced tail latency variance by ~18% and decreased hot-gpu preemption events in the sim by ~12%. Cost per token was neutral in the baseline. I can paste the experiment notebook later.

kevin: Migration plan idea: 1) introduce `scorer.v1` behind a feature flag for 2 weeks 2) enable shim that maps `latency-band` thresholds into approximate `scorer` weights for tenants 3) start light traffic canary 4) opt-in for Dedicated customers to test on their routes 5) full cutover with rollback playbook.

sam: For step 2, mapping math will be messy. We should expose a mapping table and a CLI for SRE to tweak mappings per-tenant. Prefer not to auto-translate for enterprise tenants without their approval.

maria: Agreed on opt-in for enterprise. For everyone else we can auto-translate with conservative bounds.

ops-bot: deploybot: feature-flag `unified-scorer` created by @maria.

jamie: One operational concern: telemetry. We need new metrics: scorer_score, scorer_weight_breakdown, and scored_route_choice. Also add a tag for "mapping_applied=true|false" to compare.

kevin: Add to that: a daily regression check that asserts p99 latency doesn’t increase >5% for any tenant during canary windows. If breached -> auto-roll back the flag for that tenant.

sam: How about API surface? Will customers still be able to set `latency_band` in route config?

maria: Yes for now. We'll accept both fields: `latency_band` (deprecated) and `route_scoring` (new). If both present, we log a deprecation warning and apply `route_scoring` precedence. We'll include a linter in Console to highlight deprecated fields.

jamie: Implementation note: keep mapping code isolated in routing-service, not policy-eval library, so policies remain pure and testable.

kevin: Agree. Also plan to add a feature toggle `mapping_mode` with options `strict|best-effort|disabled` for Dedicated tenants.

maria: Need owners: implementation (kevin + jamie), telemetry + alerts (jamie), customer comms + opt-in docs (sam), rollout coordination (maria). I'll open a follow-up RFC with more detail and a canary schedule.

sam: One more ask: add a small CLI tool for engs to run the mapping locally: input tenant yaml -> output translated scorer config. Saves a ton of back-and-forth.

kevin: will prototype the CLI. Plan to add a unit test matrix for 6 representative tenant profiles.

maria: Great, timeline suggestion: prototype + tests (2w), feature-flag rollout to staging (1w), small canary (1w), enterprise opt-ins (2w), full cutover (1w). Total ~7w. Open to compressing.

jamie: LGTM. Please add the acceptance criteria in the RFC: metrics thresholds, rollback conditions, and documentation checklist.

maria: Will do. Thanks all :thumbsup:
